CHECK 1 — goal: establish what the four frozen bundles share and where they differ, before ranking.
READ: all four evidence bundles (6f9f3944ba78d62b successor-anchor-l2-poincare-sinkhorn-v1; 442c7bd52814c269 fine-residual-behaviour-geodesic-transport-v1; adeb64486765c2fd poincare_residual_direction_sinkhorn_v1; 65930410bd2f75d8 bgcd-fine-v1).
SHARED: [E1]-[E3] all PROPOSED but train-only and clearly specified (directed successor counts, PPMI or row-normalised weights, successor centroids/anchors from training split only, stop-grad item table). [E5] OK 115582 distinct directed edges, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526 -> behaviour signal exists but is thin per item (~5 successors), which matters for the anchors' |S_i|<2 fallback and for bgcd/hub-noise risk. [E6] OK same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted_null 0.067 -> the frozen baseline's SIDs carry only a very weak successor signal, so behaviour-based prefix-predictability headroom is small for ALL four. [E11] geometry operator valid (log/exp error 2.78e-17, kappa=1 valid) but "says nothing about coupling". [E12] FAIL behaviour_dependency on the generic proxy (positive row scalar cannot move an argmin; a codeword-dependent weight moved no top-1 index) — a red flag on every candidate, and it penalises hardest the designs whose behaviour enters as an additive/offset cost term rather than moving the points themselves. [E13] PASS but weak: matched Euclidean intervention moved only 1 of top-1 indices -> expected effect sizes are small. [E14] CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN for all four: no joint-path proof; the admission check must be the implemented tree.
DIFFERENTIATORS I can ground: (a) PRIOR_WORK: only fine-residual is scored related_but_different against the hyperbolic-VQ literature (HVQ-VAE, HyperVQ); the other three are same_operator_or_path, i.e. least differentiated from existing hyperbolic quantisation. (b) LEVELS TOUCHED: successor-anchor acts only at L2 (L3 byte-identical); fine-residual, poincare_residual_direction and bgcd act at L2+L3. (c) SIGN/OPERATOR: successor-anchor subtracts d^2(anchor,c_k)/m_i — an ATTRACTIVE cohesion-style term, the same sign as the L1 reward that produced the rejected round's 955 L2 prefixes / 0.771 collision; fine-residual is a Mobius (isometric) transport of the residual (bijection on the ball, so it structurally cannot map two distinct residuals onto one codeword); bgcd displaces the CODE point by the same vector for all k (by the Poincare gyro/left-translation structure effectively the mirrored residual transport, bounded by m_i <= 0.5*min_k d_P) and needs an extra forward-only epoch pass (+5-7% wall clock, the most expensive); poincare_residual_direction rotates the residual direction only and, beyond the curved cost, also RESCALES the Sinkhorn temperature eps_l = eps_base*mean(C^l)/mean(C^l_euclid), which alters the baseline solver's entropy rather than only the cost matrix — its own risk list admits the plan can go nearly hard, which is the exact failure mode the scope contract protects against. (d) SCOPE HAZARD: poincare_residual_direction's temperature rescale is the only change that reaches beyond "the cost matrix carries the curved distance and the behaviour offset"; it also writes the level index from the plan's argmax column and could be read as departing from the baseline rule.
CONCLUSION SO FAR: fine-residual v1 best (isometric transport gives a structural anti-collapse guarantee against the documented rejection mode, both fine levels, no swept con
